answer.rationale: With the primary contract expiring in 14 days and the line running at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, switching vendors (memory_c2) or deferring (memory_c5, which applied to a non-critical renewal) both raise delivery-risk exposure at the worst possible time. memory_c4 suggests renegotiation can recover real margin and improve payment terms without narrowing scope, which directly serves the 18% cost-cut mandate while memory_c1 and memory_c6 indicate incumbent continuity avoids migration risk and can still yield better pricing via multi-year terms. I want to verify memory_c4's original record before committing, since it's doing the most work in justifying that cost savings are achievable without a vendor switch or service-scope reduction. I'm treating this as a standard renegotiation cycle rather than a broad rollout since the underlying vendor relationship and delivery pipeline stay unchanged; a second-source addition (memory_c3) is a reasonable follow-up next cycle to further de-risk the constrained line, but capacity limits us to one decision now. I'm flagging downstream risk because if negotiation fails to reach acceptable terms within the 14-day window, we may be forced into a rushed switch or lapse to month-to-month status under worse conditions, and I'm not certain the market benchmarking referenced in memory_c4 still holds at today's pricing.
